articles.title: Cultivo de erva-mate une trabalho e tradição em família | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Ilópolis (RS), família Greselle cultiva cerca de 100 mil pés de erva-mate e transforma o cuidado com a terra em tradição, trabalho e momentos compartilhados.
articles.summary: Em Ilópolis (RS), família Greselle cultiva cerca de 100 mil pés de erva-mate e transforma o cuidado com a terra em tradição, trabalho e momentos compartilhados.
articles.body:
Em Ilópolis, no Rio Grande do Sul, a erva-mate faz parte da paisagem, da cultura e da rotina de muitas famílias. Na propriedade de Danilo Greselle, Clair Franzon Greselle e da filha Larissa, a planta também faz parte da história construída ao longo de três décadas.

São aproximadamente 22 hectares dedicados ao cultivo e entre 80 mil e 100 mil pés de erva-mate. Cada um deles foi plantado pela própria família, em um trabalho que começou há cerca de 30 anos e continua sendo acompanhado de perto por Danilo.

“Eu e minha esposa plantamos todos os pés, um por um. Foi tudo começando aos poucos. A gente foi fazendo, limpando, plantando e cuidando. Hoje temos uma área grande, mas foi uma construção de muitos anos. É um trabalho que exige dedicação, mas também dá muita satisfação quando a gente olha para o erval e vê tudo o que conseguiu construir” , conta Danilo.

Mesmo morando atualmente na cidade, ele mantém a rotina de trabalho na propriedade todos os dias. O cuidado com os ervais acompanha as diferentes etapas do ciclo da planta, desde a preparação do solo até a colheita.

A família trabalha exclusivamente com a erva-mate. A colheita é feita manualmente e exige conhecimento para identificar o momento adequado e preservar a planta para os próximos ciclos. Após cortados, os galhos são quebrados, organizados em feixes e transportados até as ervateiras com as quais a família mantém parceria.

Danilo conhece cada etapa desse processo e explica que o cuidado começa ainda no momento da poda. “Não dá para chegar e tirar tudo. O pé de erva-mate precisa das folhas e dos galhos para continuar se desenvolvendo. Então a gente deixa uma parte para proteger a planta e auxiliar na próxima brotação. É preciso observar o erval, conhecer a planta e entender o momento certo. Quando a gente cuida bem, ela responde. É um trabalho que vai passando de um ciclo para outro”.

A relação dos povos do Sul com a erva-mate é anterior à própria formação das atuais comunidades produtoras. O consumo da planta está ligado aos povos indígenas, especialmente os guaranis, que já utilizavam a erva-mate antes da chegada dos colonizadores.

Em Ilópolis, essa história também é preservada por meio de antigas formas de beneficiamento, como o carijo, estrutura tradicional utilizada para a secagem artesanal da erva-mate.

No processo, os ramos são colocados sobre uma estrutura de madeira, próxima ao calor do fogo, para a retirada da umidade. A prática ajuda a contar como a erva-mate era preparada antes dos processos modernos de beneficiamento e representa parte do conhecimento tradicional relacionado à cultura.

Na propriedade dos Greselle, essa tradição aparece de diferentes formas. Está no cuidado com as plantas, na forma de trabalhar a terra e também em um dos momentos mais simples e importantes do dia da família: o chimarrão.

Dentro de casa, outra parte da relação da família com a erva-mate ganha significado. Depois do almoço e também à noite, a cuia passa de mão em mão. É o momento em que Danilo, Clair e Larissa se encontram, conversam e compartilham o dia.

“Eu acho que o momento de sentar e tomar um chimarrão é uma das maiores riquezas que temos como família. É um momento sagrado. Depois do almoço, todo mundo senta e toma chimarrão. Depois da janta também. A gente pode trabalhar o dia inteiro, tem dia que eu estou trabalhando aqui e elas não estão, ou cada um está fazendo uma coisa. Mas depois da janta a gente se reúne, conversa e toma chimarrão. Então, todos os dias a gente se encontra. Se não trabalhamos juntos, na hora do chimarrão estamos juntos” , afirma Danilo.

Uma tradição que acompanha a família, também ajuda a aproximar as diferentes gerações. Para Danilo, manter esse costume vivo é uma forma de fazer com que a erva-mate continue presente na vida das pessoas.

O produtor acredita que o futuro da cultura também passa por apresentar a planta para novos públicos e ampliar as possibilidades de consumo. “Precisamos abrir novos caminhos e novos consumos. O chimarrão é uma tradição muito forte, mas a erva-mate também pode estar em outros produtos. Hoje já existem alimentos feitos com erva-mate e o chá está crescendo bastante. Existe muita coisa que pode ser desenvolvida. Eu acredito que a erva ainda tem muito espaço para conquistar e que precisamos mostrar isso para as pessoas mais novas também”.

A busca por novos usos para a erva-mate acompanha um movimento de valorização da cadeia e de ampliação dos produtos derivados da planta. Ao mesmo tempo em que preserva práticas tradicionais, o setor encontra novas formas de levar a erva para diferentes consumidores e mercados.

Essa combinação entre tradição e inovação também faz parte da história dos Greselle. Cooperado da Cresol desde maio de 2022, Danilo utilizou recursos da cooperativa para adquirir insumos e também uma caminhonete utilizada nas atividades da propriedade.

A família é atendida pela Agência Ilópolis, da Cresol Noroeste, e a relação com a cooperativa é descrita por Danilo a partir da proximidade. “Quando estou em casa, estou na minha casa. Quando vou à Cresol, também estou em casa. É muito bom, é tudo muito tranquilo. Tenho conta há muitos anos e, quando eu for embora, minha conta vai ficar na Cresol. Eu me sinto em casa. A Cresol é muito boa para trabalhar” , conta.

A erva-mate também faz Danilo pensar no futuro. Depois de dedicar décadas à propriedade, ele olha para os filhos e sabe que a próxima etapa dessa história será uma escolha da nova geração.

“Enquanto eu puder, vou tocar a propriedade. Depois, os filhos sabem. Se quiserem tocar, tudo bem. Se não quiserem, não. Para mim, tudo o que existe aqui é emprestado. Eu não sou dono. Meu pai me emprestou e eu vou emprestar para os filhos. Seria muito gratificante que alguém levasse isso adiante, porque é uma dedicação de vida. Desde fazer as mudas, limpar as terras e plantar, tudo exige muita dedicação” , analisa.

A ideia de passar a propriedade adiante não está relacionada apenas à terra. É também sobre tudo aquilo que foi aprendido ao longo dos anos: o jeito de cuidar da planta, o respeito pelos ciclos da natureza, o conhecimento sobre a colheita e, principalmente, a importância de fazer tudo isso em família.

É assim que uma tradição se mantém viva: entre uma colheita e outra, entre o conhecimento de quem aprendeu com a experiência e a curiosidade de quem ainda tem muito para aprender. E, quando a cuia começa a circular, o trabalho dá lugar à conversa. A erva-mate deixa de ser apenas produto e volta a ser aquilo que sempre foi para a família: um motivo para estar junto.

articles.title: Viva a Vanguard: campanha celebra 20 anos com histórias de quem vive seus espaços | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova campanha resgata memórias, encontros e momentos que transformaram apartamentos em lares ao longo de duas décadas de história.
articles.summary: Nova campanha resgata memórias, encontros e momentos que transformaram apartamentos em lares ao longo de duas décadas de história.
articles.body:
Ao completar 20 anos, a Vanguard escolheu comemorar de uma forma pouco convencional. Em vez de olhar para os empreendimentos que construiu ou para os números alcançados ao longo da trajetória, a marca decidiu voltar sua atenção para aquilo que acontece depois da entrega das chaves: a vida do morador.

A nova campanha, lançada para celebrar as duas décadas da construtora, traz o mote "Viva a Vanguard" . A expressão carrega um duplo significado:

É um convite para viver a experiência Vanguard, experimentar seus espaços e fazer parte de sua história.

Mas também é uma celebração, no sentido mais tradicional da palavra, como um brinde ou um "parabéns pra você" pelos 20 anos da marca.

Outra característica é que a campanha nasce de uma tradição presente nas entregas dos empreendimentos. Ao receberem as chaves de seus apartamentos, os moradores são fotografados na Central Vanguard com uma câmera instantânea, registrando o primeiro momento, aquele que marca o início de uma nova etapa de vida. A imagem se transforma em uma lembrança física daquele dia. Agora a Vanguard amplia essa narrativa.

Campanha Viva a Vanguard. — Foto: Divulgação/Vanguard.

As tradicionais polaroids dão espaço a cenas do cotidiano: amigos reunidos ao redor da mesa, noites de filmes no sofá, aniversários, encontros de família, momentos simples que transformam um imóvel em lar. A proposta parte da reflexão de que a entrega das chaves nunca foi o ponto final de uma história, mas o começo dela.

"Depois da entrega das chaves vêm os encontros, a rotina e as comemorações que transformam o espaço em parte da vida. É uma forma de homenagear tudo o que é vivido dentro de cada Vanguard" , resume a gerente de marketing, Vanessa Yamamoto.

A comunicação estará presente em meios digitais e também em peças de mídia exterior, reforçando a conexão emocional construída pela marca ao longo dos anos.

Uma marca construída a partir das pessoas

Criada em 2006 pelo Grupo Plaenge, a Vanguard nasceu com a proposta de interpretar transformações de comportamento e antecipar novas formas de morar. Ao longo dessas duas décadas, a marca ajudou a apresentar novos bairros, trouxe conceitos inéditos para Londrina e desenvolveu empreendimentos que dialogam com diferentes gerações.

A campanha dos 20 anos procura justamente valorizar este legado sob uma nova perspectiva: ela celebra as experiências construídas dentro deles.

Curtiu? Venha conhecer mais do universo Vanguard! Visite a Central de Decorados na Avenida Ayrton Senna, 815. WhatsApp: (43) 3294-1570. Acompanhe mais novidades pelo Instagram @vanguard.londrina.

articles.title: Palestinians and US journalist injured by Israeli settlers in West Bank harvest attack
articles.summary: The BBC sees masked settlers attack Palestinians trying to harvest olives, amid a surge in similar incidents.
articles.body:
Watch: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians in West Bank during olive harvest

Dozens of masked settlers have attacked Palestinians and set fire to cars and olive trees during the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank.

A BBC team witnessed one of several attacks in farmland near the Palestinian village of Abu Falah. A local official said the attacks had injured 12 Palestinians, including four dual Palestinian American citizens. A foreign journalist was also among those hurt.

Driving into the area early in the morning, we came across the first signs of the violence : a stream of cars carrying wounded Palestinian olive farmers racing out along the narrow stony track, piled high with olive picking equipment, as smoke rose from several fires nearby.

The bloodied face of Majdi Fheed peered out from the backseat of one car.

"We were getting our olive trees and almost 15 Jewish guys … started attacking us with guns, with rocks, with special weapons. They hit me on my head [and] my neck – look, I am bleeding!"

Yaser AlKam, a council member from the neighbouring village of Turmus Aya told me Majdi - an American citizen - was attacked by settlers with nail-studded sticks, and needed treatment for deep wounds on his head. His elderly mother was also injured.

Another man ferrying the injured to hospital told us that settlers had attacked them with sticks while they harvested their olives, and had burned three cars – including one of his own.

"As soon as we got to the land and put our things on the ground, they started to come, so we ran away" said a woman next to him.

Asked about the violence, a US State Department spokesperson said they were aware of the reports.

"We condemn criminal violence by any party in the West Bank and call for investigations, arrests, and convictions, of those responsible," the spokesperson said.

Watching the vehicles stream past her, 73-year-old Imm Khaldoun told me emphatically that, no matter what happened, she would always return to her land. "This is my land. It's my right [to be here]" she told me.

The UN says the past two weeks have already seen more attacks by violent Israeli settlers than during the entire harvest season last year.

Olive picking in the West Bank is now a test of speed, with trees rapidly stripped of fruit as soon as the sun rises, before violent Israeli settlers attack.

In another olive orchard nearby, we watched as dozens of farmers used power-tools to strip the trees as fast as they could – one eye on the ridge above us, where a group of settlers at a new illegal outpost had already gathered, and were watching the olive harvest below.

Standing on ladders, the Palestinian farmers worked quickly, sending streams of olives onto the plastic sheets laid out under the trees. Three villages had come together to harvest these olives, the landowner Amin Khalil, told me, as a form of protection against attack. He said his land was now surrounded by seven Jewish settlements and outposts.

All Israeli settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts – small encampments on hilltops – are illegal under Israeli law as well, but many still receive state support.

"This is a hotspot – there are seven settlements around here," Amin Khalil told me. "This year, all the people came together because when there are just a few people working alone at the edge of the village, the settlers attack. So all the families are working together today."

But the tactic doesn't work today. As we watch, dozens of settlers, all dressed in black, begin moving down the hill towards us, setting fire to several groups of olive trees.

There are shouts of panic from the Palestinian farmers, yelling for children to get out of the field. Some begin swiftly wrapping up the olives to leave.

But with large numbers of people on both sides, the confrontation stalls into an uneasy stalemate. We see settlers with slingshots hurl stones towards us, and young Palestinian men running to throw stones in return.

As Israeli forces arrive, the standoff explodes into action. Settlers begin running down towards us as the farmers swiftly retreat. Some Palestinians set off fireworks to try and push the settlers back.

American journalist Heidi Levine of the Washington Post was injured in the attack. She described how dozens of settlers ambushed her as she was reporting at the scene.

"I got jumped," she said. "I was on the ground and they were kicking me and I was trying to hold onto my camera and my bag. I had my helmet and flak jacket on which protected me. They made me stand up and they kicked me again, and this went on for at least 10 minutes."

In a statement, Washington Post executive editor Matt Murray said Levine had been clearly identifiable as a journalist.

"We are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities," he said.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said personnel had been despatched to the area "following a report of a violent confrontation". It said a female journalist had been injured during the confrontation. And that "all circumstances" surrounding the incident would be examined.

As the farmers retreated, the sound of live ammunition cracked across the fields. It was unclear if settlers or Israeli forces were firing.

Minutes later, Israeli forces began firing tear gas into the Palestinian fields to end the confrontation – a well-worn Israeli pattern of managing these conflicts.

The UN says settler attacks on the olive harvest this year have so far killed one Palestinian and injured more than 120 others across the West Bank.

Illegal Jewish outposts have mushroomed here over the past few years, clustering in closer around Palestinian olive groves.

What we witnessed was part of a pattern being repeated day after day, as settler outposts here increase.

The yearly olive harvest has become a litmus test of how the policies of Israel's fiercely pro-settlement government are affecting Palestinians here, by presiding over growing violence by extremist settlers, and fuelling Jewish claims to the land.

articles.title: What about our livelihood, ask Delhi traders as protests disrupt festive sales
articles.summary: Delhi traders in Connaught Place, Khan Market and Old Delhi protest festive sales losses from demonstrations, seek protest zones; SC hearing set for Oct 26.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: On Friday afternoon, Connaught Place once again witnessed thin footfall despite a festive season being underway. While shops remained open, protests and a heavy police presence occupied parts of the market, affecting the movement of shoppers and leaving shopkeepers and vendors worried about business during this otherwise peak season.With the weekend accounting for a major share of sales, many shopkeepers feared prolonged losses would make it difficult to pay rent, staff salaries and other expenses. A representative of Wenger’s, a well-known outlet at CP, said, “Eighty to 90% of our business happens over the weekend. In the current situation, we are not even seeing 10% of our usual customers.”A woman vendor from Gujarat, who visits CP every year to sell traditional Gujarati products, said the situation had dampened her spirits this season. “My family had asked me not to come this time, but I still came. However, there are hardly any customers,” she said.Traders at CP, Khan Market and several Old Delhi markets have expressed resentment over repeated protests in central Delhi during the festive season, alleging that road closures and restrictions on movement have severely hit business, with sales dropping to as low as 10% on the days of agitation.In fresh letters to Prime Minister, Union home minister and Delhi Police, traders reiterated that demonstrations be shifted from major commercial hubs as frequent protests were depriving them of crucial sales. Several traders’ associations have also approached Supreme Court, seeking relief. The court has scheduled the matter for Oct 26.In an appeal issued late Thursday night to all parties and protesters, New Delhi Traders Association (NDTA) said, “We respect your right to protest..., but CP is not your stage, it’s our workplace.” A poster shared by it on X stated, “You protest for a better tomorrow, don’t kill our today.”NDTA president Atul Bhargava said just after CJP’s ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ Friday, another demonstration was organised by the INDIA bloc, adding to their woes. “We have to pay our rentals, staff, property tax. We are incurring heavy losses,” he said.Arguing that CP is a major commercial and traffic hub connecting north and south Delhi, Bhargava said protesters should use designated demonstration sites.Responding to a post by CJP’s Abhijit Dipke on X that businesses suffer when govt shuts down a city, suspends internet services or restricts movement, rather than because of peaceful protests, Bhargava said traders’ concerns stemmed from their past experiences, when “such protests turn out to be violent and traders suffer automatically”.Delhi Kirana Committee and Khan Market Traders’ Association are among the bodies that have filed petitions. KMTA president Sanjiv Mehra said all entry points to Khan Market from Nizamuddin, India Habitat Centre, Safdarjung and Race Course had been closed. He said Supreme Court had indicated Friday that traders could be compensated if it found they had been unlawfully deprived of business because of Tiranga Yatra.In a letter to Prime Minister, Rajendra Kapoor, vice-president of Delhi Vyapar Mahasangh, said markets such as Sadar bazaar, Chandni Chowk, Khari Baoli, Bhagirath Palace, Kashmere Gate and Qutab Road served buyers from across the country. “Traffic congestion and restrictions can prevent customers from reaching shops, affecting business beyond the immediate protest site.”Paramjeet Singh Pamma, president of Sadar bazaar Bari Market Traders Association, said inflation had already put traders under pressure. “Adding to our woes are these protests. If goods purchased in advance for the festive season are not sold on time, traders risk having their working capital tied up, increasing their financial burden.”Vinay Thakur, general secretary of Palika Bazaar Market Shopkeepers’ Association, said shopkeepers were experiencing their second consecutive weekend of disruption. “What about our right to earn a livelihood?”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Ahead of polls, Amit Shah attacks Mann govt for drug menace
articles.summary: NEW DELHI/CHANDIGARH: Union home minister Amit Shah on Friday said the Centre will seek Punjab govt's response over two incidents in the state: a father
articles.body: NEW DELHI/CHANDIGARH: Union home minister Amit Shah on Friday said the Centre will seek Punjab govt's response over two incidents in the state: a father consuming poison under pressure in Dirba and the broad daylight killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa.In a post on microblogging site X, Shah said Punjab is today grappling with a rising threat of drugs, gangsterism and organised crime. He asked chief minister Bhagwant Mann who will ultimately bear the responsibility for the safety of Punjab's people."In Dirba, a father succumbing to pressure and consuming poison, and in Mansa, the broad-daylight murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota -- who had raised his voice against drugs -- have raised serious questions about the law and order situation in Punjab," Shah's post read.Political parties, including the BJP, have been increasingly highlighting the drug issue in poll-bound Punjab, where assembly elections are due early next year.In his X post, Shah said, "In Punjab, the drug trade is flourishing, the threat of organised crime is growing, and questions are being raised about the safety of those who speak out against drugs."Addressing chief minister Mann, Shah said the people of Punjab want results, not publicity."Bhagwant Mann ji, the people of Punjab do not want promises, they want answers; not announcements, but results; decisive strikes against drug networks; and an impartial investigation into any political patronage received by criminals."Today, I reiterate my pledge before the people of Punjab that when our government comes to power in Punjab, we will work with full force to create a drug-free, gangster-free, and secure Punjab. Our goal is clear: strikes against the drug trade, protection of our youth's future, strict action against criminals, and the rule of law in such a way that no citizen is forced to live under the shadow of fear," the home minister said.Reacting sharply to Shah's post, Mann pointed to a drug seizure at a Gujarat port and said the home minister should to "take responsibility" for his own duties.In an X post in Punjabi, Mann said, "Amit Shah ji, you should have consulted with your advisors before speaking about me. The BSF (Border Security Force) has jurisdiction over a 50-kilometre range. 3,000 kg of 'chitta' (synthetic drugs) are being seized at the Kandla port in Gujarat. Before blaming Bhagwant Mann, take responsibility for your own duties. Do not simply copy-paste tweets drafted for your sycophants." PTIGet the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Forgotten American 'cure-all' from 1903 makes comeback with one key ingredient missing
articles.summary: A papaya-based aperitif born from a forgotten homeopathic remedy was revived after a chance discovery at a state park. Its founders tell Fox News Digital how the drink found new life.
articles.body: A forgotten American elixir once marketed as a "cure-all" more than a century ago has gotten a second life — thanks to a chance discovery in Florida. Munyon's Paw-Paw, an alcoholic beverage dating to the early 1900s, has been resurrected by two longtime spirits industry veterans who stumbled upon its unusual history during a family outing. Jupiter, Florida, resident Joe Colucci was visiting John D. MacArthur Beach State Park in Palm Beach County when he spotted an antique bottle from 1903 in a display about Dr. James Munyon, a businessman who once owned a nearby island. GEORGE WASHINGTON'S 1757 BEER RECIPE BROUGHT BACK TO LIFE Intrigued, Colucci called his longtime colleague, Paul Massey, and the two began digging into the forgotten drink's past. What they discovered was a colorful chapter of American history. Munyon, an entrepreneur who built a fortune selling homeopathic remedies around the turn of the 20th century, marketed his Paw-Paw elixir as a medicinal cure-all. The original concoction contained fermented papaya and alcohol — along with a surprising ingredient, according to the founders. COCA-COLA QUIETLY AXED ONE REAGAN-ERA DRINK THAT DISAPPEARED FROM STORE SHELVES "There was actually THC in the original formulation as well," Massey told Fox News Digital. The pair traveled to Pennsylvania to meet with a historian researching Munyon's life and eventually obtained an original bottle containing some of the century-old liquid. They even sampled it. "Wasn't exactly still fresh, to say the least," Colucci recalled. Determined to revive the historic brand, the entrepreneurs worked with a Miami craft distiller to develop a modern version inspired by the original, minus the THC. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Launched in 2023, today's Munyon's Paw-Paw is a 20% alcohol-by-volume apéritif featuring 14 natural ingredients, including papaya, orange, grapefruit and hibiscus — botanicals the founders say were once grown on Munyon's island. Even the bottle pays tribute to the past. "When we saw the original bottle, we thought, 'Man, we could just run with that,'" Colucci said. "So, ours is a replica. That package almost tells the story." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS For the founders, resurrecting Munyon's Paw-Paw is about more than bringing another alcoholic beverage to market. It's about preserving a forgotten piece of American ingenuity at a time when nostalgia and old-fashioned brands continue to capture consumers' attention. "Americans just want to hear a great piece of U.S. history, and we're bringing that back with our product," Massey said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Although the original was sold as medicine, the modern version has a decidedly more recreational purpose. articles.title: Yemen’s government says Houthis fired two missiles at Aden airport
articles.summary: Attack comes as Yemeni gov’t forces claim advances in Marib and say they ‘neutralised’ 430 Houthi fighters in 24 hours.
articles.body:
Yemen’s internationally recognised government says the Houthis have launched missiles at the airport in Aden, a day after carrying out a deadly attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city.

Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said two missiles landed near the runway at Aden International Airport on Friday, 500 metres (1,640 feet) from an aircraft that was preparing to take off.

All passengers and crew were safe, he said on X, thanking “divine providence” for preventing a potential “horrific humanitarian catastrophe” and calling the attacks on the airport “a grave violation of international laws and norms”.

The Houthis, in a statement attributed to a military source, said on Friday that they launched an attack on “the Saudi forces’ command headquarters in the Badr camp in Aden province” as well as a weapons depot, the AFP news agency reported.

The latest attack in Aden, which is the seat of the internationally recognised government, comes amid continued heavy fighting in Yemen’s reignited civil war between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-aligned Houthis.

Yemeni government forces said earlier on Friday that troops had advanced in Marib province northeast of Sanaa.

Military spokesman Majed al-Nazili said Yemeni government forces, with air support, had made significant “territorial gains” in the eastern part of the province, securing “key positions”.

He also said Yemeni forces had “neutralised” more than 430 Houthi fighters in 24 hours, while destroying or disabling more than 100 of their vehicles and military assets.

Elsewhere, in Taiz governorate, which has emerged as a key battlefront in the war, Yemeni government forces claimed to have fended off several “large-scale” Houthi attacks, inflicting “heavy losses” on the group.

Yemeni government forces also claimed to have captured a specialised drone team affiliated with the Houthis in the Taiz area.

In recent weeks, Houthi forces have encircled the city of Taiz — Yemen’s third largest urban centre — by ⁠cutting its main road south to Aden, causing widespread ⁠displacement and worsening a humanitarian crisis.

Elsewhere on Friday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said it had downed missiles and drones over Riyadh and other parts of Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia has accused Iran of encouraging Houthi attacks against the kingdom, including by arming and training the group.

But Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday rejected the accusation, saying Tehran had not played a role in any Houthi operations. The ministry also reiterated a proposal to mediate between the Houthis and Riyadh.

The war in Yemen erupted in 2014 when the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), seized the capital, Sanaa, and forced the government to flee.

An international military coalition led by Saudi Arabia intervened in support of the internationally recognised government in 2015, leading to years of fighting between the warring sides.

A 2022 UN-backed truce halted most fighting, but tensions have been high in Yemen since the Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabian ports and shipping passing through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in July.

In September, the Houthis carried out a lightning ground offensive on Mocha, pushing back forces loyal to Yemen’s government from the Red Sea port city.

The same month, the group’s forces again swept through and seized territory along the western coast and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, including the strategically located Mayyun Island in the strait.

articles.title: New wildfire in Southern California explodes in size, burning multiple homes
articles.summary: The Norte Fire began just after noon Friday and has quickly grown to 465 acres, the Orange County Fire Authority said. It’s one of several fires burning amid fierce Santa Ana winds affecting Southern California.
articles.body: A fast-moving wildfire in Southern California quickly consumed hundreds of acres and burned multiple homes after sparking in Orange County Friday, county officials said. The Norte Fire began around noon Friday near a San Clemente residential area and has quickly grown to more than 450 acres, the Orange County Fire Authority said. It’s one of several fires that have broken out since Thursday amid fierce Santa Ana winds affecting Southern California. Topography and weather conditions allowed the fire to grow rapidly, Orange County Division 3 Fire Chief Mark Backoff said in a video posted to social media Friday afternoon. Six homes have been destroyed or damaged by the fire, Backoff said. One firefighter experienced heat exhaustion. “We continue engaged in the fire fight and have additional resources coming at this point,” he said. Aerial footage from CNN affiliate KCBS showed multiple houses burning Friday afternoon. Five zones in San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano were under evacuation orders while surrounding areas had evacuation warnings in effect. Evacuation shelters have been opened at community centers in both San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano, Orange County fire officials said. Resident Robert Morris called the sudden threat to homes “a wake-up call,” telling KCBS, “I’ve lived here since 1995, and this is the first time we’ve really ever had a fire in this area.” Orange County sheriff’s deputies were going door to door in areas under evacuation order telling people to leave for their safety, Sgt. Lizbeth Gwisdalla, a spokesperson for the sheriff’s department, told CNN. Ten schools were dismissed early “out of an abundance of caution” and sports and after-school programs were canceled, Capistrano Unified School District announced. Wind gusts in the area are reaching 25 mph. Winds are expected to remain elevated until this evening, when they could begin to die down in areas closer to the coast beginning around 7 p.m. local time. The Santa Ana winds peak Friday but will remain elevated through Saturday, and then diminishing over the weekend. Several fires have broken out since Santa Ana winds began Thursday, forcing evacuations in other areas of Southern California. In Malibu, more than 7,000 structures were in areas under evacuation orders or warnings on Friday because of the Bryson Fire, which has burned roughly 150 acres and is just 17% contained since starting Thursday evening, a Los Angeles County Fire spokesperson told CNN, estimating the number of people under evacuation order to be in the hundreds. Crews made “great progress” against the fire overnight, Los Angeles County Fire Chief Anthony Marrone said during a news conference Friday morning. At least one firefighter had “minor injuries” and was taken to the hospital, he said. The chief did not provide additional details except to say, “They’ve been on the line all night, so minor injuries are expected.” The fire is still threatening more than 100 structures in the area, but no damages have been reported. “But obviously, if the winds kick up later this afternoon and we were to lose containment of the fire, a larger area could be affected and under threat,” the chief said. Over 400 firefighters and more than 75 “ground and aerial resources” are committed to the Bryson Fire, he said. This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: Immigrant ICE was seeking when its agent hit a man with its SUV has been dead since 2017, family says
articles.summary: An immigrant rights group is calling for ICE to “come clean” about its pursuit of Jose Parra Hernández and to release bodycam video.
articles.body: The person ICE said it was trying to detain when one of its agents struck a man with an SUV in Houston last weekend has been dead since 2017, according to an immigration advocacy group and an attorney who spoke with the deceased immigrant’s family. ICE said that its agents were “conducting a targeted enforcement operation” to arrest Jose Mendoza-Cervantes when an agent hit and seriously injured Miguel Parra Hernández, 48, on Oct. 10. In a previous statement, ICE said it attempted a vehicle stop and the two people in the car ran away. The officers tried to apprehend the fleeing men, and “Miguel Parra Hernandez ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck,” the ICE spokesperson stated. The collision left Parra with hip, leg and ankle injuries, including a broken leg, according to his family and representatives. Afterward, ICE issued a statement that included a headshot of the man it identified as Mendoza-Cervantes with the word “wanted” in capital white letters. But the daughter of the man identified by ICE as Mendoza-Cervantes told an immigrant civil rights group that the photo was actually of her deceased father. In a news conference Friday, the leader of FIEL Houston, Cesar Espinosa, said the daughter had identified the man in the photo as his father, José Hector Jimenez Mendoza, who passed away almost a decade ago while trying to enter the United States. “She called our office sobbing because she saw her dad’s picture all over the news, all over the ICE website, saying they were looking for her dad,” Espinosa said. He added FIEL has turned over all relevant documents to Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare. The New York Times first reported that Mendoza had died in 2017, stating that Mendoza’s daughter, Jamie Jimenez told the outlet the family was “horrified” to see their dad shown as a fugitive who was alive. She told the newspaper he used aliases, including the one used by ICE. Parra’s attorney, Kim Bruno, provided a copy of a Mexican death certificate given to her and FIEL by the family. It lists the man’s name as J. Hector Jimenez Mendoza, his death year as 2017 and the location of death as Laredo, Texas. Several sections of the death certificate, which contains identities of parents as well as addresses and cause of death, were blacked out. Bruno said the news that the man ICE identified as Mendoza-Cervantes is dead is “beyond mind-blowing” and the use of the dead man’s image is “jaw-dropping.” Espinosa slammed ICE at the press conference and accused the agency of misidentifying the man with Parra. “Either someone is not telling the truth or, all of a sudden, the two ICE agents have developed a sixth sense and are able to see dead people,” said Espinosa. Espinosa called on ICE “to tell the truth. Come clean and turn over all body cameras.” A senior Department of Homeland Security official told NBC News on Thursday it had bodycam video it was reviewing internally but a decision had not been made about releasing it. At the press conference, Espinosa introduced the other man who fled with Parra, who identified himself only as “Omar.” He wouldn’t take questions but confirmed he was the person in the car with Parra before they fled on foot. The man has light-colored eyes, unlike the man in the picture that ICE issued. ICE and the Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to questions regarding Jimenez Mendoza and about Espinosa’s comments. Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare is investigating ICE on a possible aggravated assault with a deadly weapon charge as a result of Parra’s injury. Teare, a Democrat, said it is “pretty obvious” from videos that ICE intentionally struck and ran over Parra. ICE has stated that “allegations that ICE struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are RECKLESS and FALSE.” Teare said he could take the case to a grand jury as soon as next week. A senior DHS official told NBC News on Thursday that the officer driving the vehicle that hit Parra has been placed on administrative leave. Bruno also is representing Luis Delfín Martínez, one of two men who were handcuffed in the back of the ICE vehicle when it struck Parra. The two men had been arrested in a separate operation, Bruno and Espinosa said previously. Delfín, Parra and the second man in the vehicle, José Presa Cañada, are undocumented, Espinosa said. Bruno said on Friday that Delfín suffered soft-tissue injuries from being tossed around the back of the ICE vehicle while he was handcuffed and not buckled in as it pursued Parra. Delfín is being detained in the Montgomery Processing Center in Conroe, Texas. ICE did not immediately respond to a question about the allegations regarding Delfín. Teare told NBC News on Thursday that his office had interviewed Presa at a south Texas detention center close to the border, and obtained “a significant amount of relevant details from him.” ICE had told Teare’s office that it was planning to deport Presa, Teare said.

articles.title: Ulster University: £800,000 spent on scrapped sports dome plans
articles.summary: Ulster University has also revealed the multi-million pound dome would have cost a further £1m to run each year.
articles.body:
A Northern Ireland university spent £800,000 on a planned indoor sports dome in Londonderry before the project was scrapped.

Plans for Ulster University's (UU) multimillion pound dome, which was to house multiple sports, including rugby, football and Gaelic games, were first announced in 2024.

But in August UU axed the project saying it was no longer financially viable.

The university, which earlier this year announced it needed to make savings of about £25m and would be making up to 450 staff redundant, has revealed it spent hundreds of thousands of pounds on the dome project before it was axed.

UU said, in response to a Freedom of Information request from BBC Radio Foyle's Mark Patterson Show, that approximately £700,000 had been spent "on project-related activities".

Project management and governance arrangements cost the university a further £100,000, UU said.

SDLP assembly member Sinéad McLaughlin told BBC Radio Foyle the dome had been announced to "much fanfare" but it had become clear the dome was an "unaffordable project".

"But my problem is that there is legitimate questions about how we reach the position after spending £800,000," she said.

McLaughlin added: "It does seem a lot of money to be spent before they came to the conclusion that it was unviable and financially unsustainable."

The Foyle MLA said it was unfortunate "it took so long to get to that point."

According to the UU figures given to BBC Radio Foyle, the overall costs to build the dome had spiralled from an initial £16.8m to £20.1m at the time the project was scrapped

It further said that as a commercial entity the dome would have cost in excess of £1m in running costs annually.

McLaughlin said with the higher education sector in Northern Ireland in financial crisis there was "is no way that Ulster University could have sustained the upkeep of that dome."

When plans for the indoor sports arena were first announced, the 15,000 square metres (3.7 acres) dome, was described as "game-changing" for Derry.

UU said as well as hosting sport, the dome would also host community and musical events, adding it was "a first-of-its-scale facility for Northern Ireland".

It was being part funded by the international PeacePlus programme - jointly supported by the European Union, the UK government, the Irish government and Stormont - which was to provide €10.86m (£9.16m).

In their Freedom of Information response, UU said its proposed contribution to the dome was to be £8.3m.

At the time the university announced the dome would not go ahead, UU said the decision not to proceed with the project was "an inevitable consequence" of the "lack of a sustainable funding model for higher education" in Northern Ireland.

The Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB) told BBC News NI that no PeacePlus funding had been paid.

It said it was working on options on how the funding will be reallocated "and remain committed to delivering impactful projects for communities across the area and throughout Northern Ireland and the border counties of Ireland".

It added it could not give a commitment that any reallocation will be in the north-west.

articles.title: Recovering from lung surgery, Pope Leo urges Putin to agree to ceasefire in Russian-held Ukraine city
articles.summary: Pope Leo called Vladimir Putin from his hospital bed to urge a ceasefire in Oleshky, Ukraine, where food deliveries have been blocked since May.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV called Russian President Vladimir Putin while recovering from surgery in the hospital to urge him to call a ceasefire in the city of Oleshky in Ukraine. "During the conversation, the Holy Father expressed his deep concern about the grave humanitarian situation in the city of Oleshky, in the Kherson region, and called for a ceasefire to allow the delivery of food and medical assistance and the voluntary and safe evacuation of the civilian population," the Vatican said in a statement. "Finally, the Holy Father reaffirmed the Holy See’s commitment to promoting dialogue and peace." TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE ENERGY CEASEFIRE BETWEEN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE The situation in Oleshky is dire with no humanitarian food deliveries allowed in the Russian-controlled city since May. It also has no electricity, gas or running water, and the hospital is barely functional. The pope was diagnosed with lung cancer Tuesday and underwent a procedure to remove the lower lobe of his right lung. The 71-year-old remained in the hospital recovering on Friday but seemed to be doing well. Along with the call, he held Mass in a makeshift hospital chapel, and the Vatican released the first images of him since his surgery, which showed him standing at an altar. POPE LEO XIV SEEN FOR FIRST TIME SINCE LUNG CANCER SURGERY AMID MAJOR RECOVERY MILESTONE His doctors said he showed "continued improvement." "His post-operative recovery allows him to carry out his normal daily activities completely on his own," a medical update signed by his personal physician, Luigi Carbone, and the head of thoracic surgery at Gemelli, Dr. Stefano Margaritora, said. The pope is expected to deliver his traditional Angelus prayer service on Sunday either from the hospital or the Vatican. articles.title: Halloween costumes 2026: From Obsession to Odyssey, the top TV, film and pop culture party outfits
articles.summary: Freaky Nikki, Dolly Parton and whimsical costumes like gargoyles are popular among adults dressing up this year.
articles.body:
If you're still on the hunt for the perfect Halloween costume, then you might want to look to gargoyles, Freaky Nikki and Dolly Parton for inspiration - they are all predicted to be popular outfit choices for 2026.

"People don't necessarily want to look frightening - they want to look extraordinary," says costume designer Tamar Zaig, who runs a fancy dress hire shop in London and says she's seeing a "real appetite for escapism, glamour and a bit of dark humour" right now.

And as usual, the year's major film and TV releases, as well as news and pop culture trends, are also driving outfit choices.

The Traitors is a timely choice, with host Claudia Winkleman's look easy to pull together. Think fringe, tartan, chunky knitwear and some heavy eyeliner.

Winkleman is "a classic that we see every year", says the creator behind the popular Love of Huns Instagram account (who did not want to be named). But she "will definitely be making a return this Halloween off the back of all the Traitors love and the icon that she is".

Ice hockey romance series Off Campus also features in many of the outfit inspiration videos trending online.

The show's main characters, Dean and Allie attend a Halloween party in the series, with Allie dressed as J-Lo and Dean as Top Gun's Maverick , which could provide a rather meta costume opportunity for fans or couples.

Another of this year's most popular TV shows, Widow's Bay - which scooped up at this year's Emmy Awards - is also inspiring outfits.

Maria Nichol, 35, a horror aficionado from Ely in Cambridgeshire, plans to dress as Kate O'Flynn's character Patricia - and is trying to replicate her gothic headdress, which includes antlers and a taxidermy fox, by crafting her own from foam clay, foil and fur.

One of the most replicated outfits looks set to be Nikki from indie horror film phenomenon Obsession , say fancy dress shops, influencers and make-up artists.

The character's red and black zebra print top went viral earlier this year, selling out online and reportedly leading to a 27,000-person waitlist before returning to stores.

"We've had customers asking for Nikki," says Muhammad Rai from shop Fancy Dress Town in London, with people trying to recreate her with a red corset and wig, "although unfortunately, we currently have none in stock".

"I've had a few people ask me to do that make-up for them," adds special effects make-up artist and prosthetics designer Meg, from Liverpool.

Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Practical Magic

We might also see a surge in 1990s and 2000s nostalgia, believes Nichol, with party-goers dressed as Buffy, Hilary Duff and characters from Practical Magic, after the film's sequel was released last month.

Wuthering Heights, The Bride! and The Odyssey

As well as Obsession, some of this year's other top grossing films – such as the Michael Jackson biopic, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey – are also on the cards.

"I'm seeing a lot of Gothic romance and historical influences not only in films such as Wuthering Heights, The Odyssey and The Bride!, but in fashion too, with corsets, lace, dramatic silhouettes appearing on the catwalks, particularly at London Fashion Week," says designer Zaig.

"Along with Peaky Blinders, I think these kind of productions have brought some great theatrical costume styles back into the spotlight, from elaborate period gowns and Greek mythology to 1930s glamour."

Classic horror franchises such as Scream and Scary Movie (Scream 7 and Scary Movie 6 were both released this year), should also not be overlooked, say fancy dress shops.

Ghost face masks from Scream have made up 30% of sales at Hollywood Fancy Dress in Bournemouth, says the shop's head manager Ben Cook.

Meanwhile, characters from hit series Wednesday and Bridgerton are likely to make a return. And outfits from KPop Demon Hunters – which won best animated film at this year's Oscars - are the current biggest seller for children, according to Cook.

It's not just fictional characters who might be joining your Halloween night out.

"I also expect to see plenty of instantly recognisable personalities, from the iconic Dolly Parton with her extravagant wigs and rhinestones to political figures such as Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin," says Zaig.

Rai from Fancy Dress Town also says blonde wigs, cowboy-style waistcoats and microphones are in high demand, following the death of Parton aged 80 in August.

Meanwhile, pop icons Charli XCX and Madonna could make a good duo costume, suggests Love of Huns, following the pair's collaboration on remix Danceteria Afterhours.

"Both have had enough iconic looks between them, so there's plenty to work with."

Other fresh pop culture references could include Mariah Carey and The Last Supper, after the star became a meme for sharing a selfie with the Leonardo da Vinci painting in Milan, they add. It's "a strong option" that "requires very little arts and crafts ability" – "a blonde wig and an A3 piece of card with The Last Supper printed on it and you're pretty much there".

"Low effort, high impact, and the sort of costume that makes absolutely no sense to anyone who hasn't been keeping up with online pop culture."

Or another option that could make people smile is the ready-to-drink cocktail brand Buzzballz, Love of Huns suggests. "We know it's been done before, but dressing up as your favourite flavour is a fab opportunity to show off a bit of creativity."

And if you want to try something a little different...

The whimsical fashion trend, which has dominated social media feeds in 2026, is also predicted to be a big influence this Halloween for women. Think gargoyles, moths, mushrooms, woodland fairies and 17th Century Pierrot clowns.

In keeping with the theme, Lauren Sidebottom, a TikTok beauty and fashion creator from Leeds, is planning on dressing up as a weeping angel.

The 23-year-old, who studied theatrical makeup at college, says she'll be creating the look using body paint, grey tights, a cracking makeup effect on her skin, drawn-on tears, and a grey wig.

Women her age are, she says "wanting to look cool, different, not like every other girl," with their whimsical costumes.

Tiggy Bellinger, 21, from West Sussex, agrees DIY costumes can help avoid people wearing "the exact same thing".

She has also been sharing whimsical Halloween looks online, including a mime artist, the Very Hungry Caterpillar and a ladybird.

She uses clothes she already has or can borrow, and a bit of creative DIY, to create her looks, with the aim of encouraging others to do the same instead of buying ready-made outfits from fast fashion retailers.

"The fun thing about making costumes and Halloween is the creativity and finding bits and pieces that match and, you know, making things," she says.

This is also the case for Sophia, 25, who lives in Cambridge and is using a long blonde wig and pink dress she already owns to dress up as Hannah Montana, to chime with this year's anniversary special.

"Even if you just notice that you have one colour, like, 'Wow I have a lot of purple' or 'I have a lot of this sparkly material that I don't get to wear often', and thinking about what characters or what object even that that could remind you of, I think you could get something really creative that other people wouldn't have."

articles.title: Panchang Today, October 17, 2026: Shukla Paksh 7 (Saptami), Mula, Shubh Muhurat, Rahu Kaal and More

articles.body: Panchang Today is that steady daily guide many of us rely on, whether we are stepping out for work, starting a study plan, or simply trying to keep the home atmosphere peaceful. Rooted in the spiritual wisdom of the Hindu calendar, it helps you read the day with a little more precision, not just by the clock, but by the Moon’s mood too. It’s also a simple way to stay connected to cultural roots while making mindful choices about money, words, and timing. Some days feel like open skies, some like shifting winds. Below are the important Panchang details for October 17, 2026 for India: Date & Day Details Date & Day DetailsSaturday carries its own weight. It asks for discipline, honest effort, and a practical mind that doesn’t get carried away by impulse. On this day, the Moon sits in a growing phase, and that matters because the Shukla Paksha pushes life forward, like a sapling reaching for light.The Tithi is Shukla Paksh 7 (Saptami), and it stays in force until 08:28:23, after which Shukla Paksh 8 (Ashtami) begins. Saptami is a day of steady rising energy. It supports progress that is earned, not rushed. Think of tasks where consistency matters, like building a new habit, following up on pending emails, clearing a backlog at work, or committing to a health routine. Since this Saptami ends early, the first part of the morning holds the strongest Saptami flavour. If you’ve been delaying something simple, like submitting a form, tidying a corner of the house, or finally having a calm talk with a family member, do it before the day becomes noisy. After 08:28:23, Ashtami brings a sharper edge. It can amplify determination, but also impatience if you let it.Nakshatra is Mula until 09:47:15, after which P.Asadha takes over. Mula’s presiding deity is Nirriti, linked with uprooting and getting to the root of things. This is not the star for pretty cover-ups. It’s the star that says, “What’s the real reason?” Perfect for decluttering, ending unhealthy habits, auditing spending, or having the tough but necessary conversation. Mula can feel intense, like pulling out weeds that have grown deep. Yet it gives relief after the pulling is done. Once P.Asadha arrives after 09:47:15, the tone becomes more about steady victory through patience and effort. It’s like shifting from digging the soil to planting properly.The Moon sign is Sagittarius 11.26, and it transitions at 18/10/2026 19:33:05 into Capricorn. Sagittarius Moon days often bring big-picture thinking. You may feel hopeful, talkative, and eager to “sort everything out at once”. Good, but don’t overpromise. Keep your plans realistic, and your words measured, especially with elders or coworkers.Yoga is Atiganda until 23:02:48, then Sukarma follows. Atiganda can make the day feel a little knotty, like small obstacles that test your patience. It’s not meant to stop you, it’s meant to slow you down so you act with care. Karan influences the working rhythm too. Gara runs until 19:11:40, supportive for steady tasks and routine progress. Vanij continues until 08:28:23, good for trade and practical dealings, but you’ll still want to be cautious because the day mixes both supportive and challenging signals. Read that as a reminder. Do what’s necessary, but do it with your eyes open.Auspicious Timings (Shubh Muhurat)Auspicious Timings (Shubh Muhurat)If you want the day to cooperate, choose your windows like you choose the right lane in traffic. The Brahma Muhurta from 04:17:26 to 05:07:22 is quiet, pure, and mentally powerful. This is the best time for prayer, mantra, study, or simply sitting with your own thoughts before the world starts calling. Even 20 minutes here can clean up your mood for hours.Pratah Sandhya runs from 04:42:24 to 05:57:18. It’s suited for morning rituals, a bath, Surya arghya, and setting intentions. Your mind is more receptive at this time, and small promises you make to yourself actually stick.Abhijit Muhurta is from 11:20:14 to 12:06:22. Use it for important calls, approvals, interviews, signing routine papers, or starting a focused work sprint. Abhijit is like a short patch of clear sky when the day’s energies feel scattered.Vijay Muhurta runs from 13:38:38 to 14:24:46. As the name suggests, it supports success through effort. Pick this for competitive tasks, presentations, negotiating a timeline with your team, or taking a bold but sensible step. This is also a good time to push a stuck project forward.Godhuli Muhurta is from 17:29:10 to 17:54:08, that sacred twilight when day and night exchange places. It’s ideal for lamp lighting, family prayer, and gentle reconciliation. If the home atmosphere has been tense, this is a sweet window to soften it.Sayahana Sandhya extends from 17:29:10 to 18:44:04, supportive for evening worship, gratitude practice, and calming the mind after a demanding day. Nishita Muhurta comes late, from 23:18:42 to 00:08:38, traditionally used for deeper sadhana. If you can’t do a full ritual, even quiet japa or a short reading works.Ravi Yoga appears from 05:57:18 to 09:46:19, often considered helpful for constructive actions and confidence. Still, keep the day’s overall tone in mind and choose grounded tasks.Choghadiya also gives useful cues. During the day, Shubh @ 07:23, Laabh @ 13:09, and Amrit @ 14:36 are supportive periods to schedule your better work, your important meetings, or any purchase you’ve already decided on. At night, Laabh @ 17:29, Shubh @ 20:36, Amrit @ 22:09, and Laabh @ 28:23 can be used for calm family time, study, planning, and prayer.Inauspicious Timings Inauspicious TimingsRahu Kaal is the first caution flag for many households, and today it falls from 08:49 to 10:16. This is the stretch to avoid starting new ventures, making major financial decisions, or signing contracts. Rahu’s energy can create confusion and false confidence. During this period, keep things routine. If you must work, focus on what’s already ongoing, like clearing pending tasks, organising files, or replying to messages without committing to anything new.For inner balance, Rahu Kaal is a fine time for spiritual protection. Sit for a few minutes, breathe slowly, and chant the Rahu mantra “Om Raam Rahave Namaha”. Even 11 repetitions done with attention can settle the mind. Don’t fight the energy, channel it.The Panchang also notes rahu_kaal from 08:50:16 to 10:16:45. Treat this as the same caution zone, extending your care a little on both sides if your schedule allows.Gulika Kaal is marked as gulkai_kaal from 05:57:18 to 07:23:47. Gulika time is not ideal for fresh starts, especially for purchases or launching something new. It’s better for routine duties. Get ready for the day, travel if needed, but avoid dramatic announcements.Yamaganda runs from 13:09:43 to 14:36:12. This is another time to avoid initiating important actions. If you’ve been meaning to confront someone, pause. Words can turn sharp here, and you may regret the tone.Dur Muhurtam is from 07:29:34 to 08:15:34. Avoid risky travel decisions, avoid impulsive spending, and avoid sending that emotionally charged message. Wait, sip some water, read it again.Varjyam falls from 20:36:33 to 22:24:43. This is a classic “don’t force it” period. Skip big commitments, skip heavy discussions, and don’t pressure family members for immediate answers. Let the night breathe.Baana is noted from 05:57:18 to 19:52:18, suggesting a long stretch where you should remain careful and intentional. Visha Yoga appears briefly from 05:55:18 to 05:56:18. Keep that minute simple, no rushing out in agitation.One interesting mix today is that vidaal_yoga runs from 05:57:18 to 09:46:19, while Ravi Yoga is also from 05:57:18 to 09:46:19. What does that mean in daily life? Don’t gamble with fate. Use the supportive side for honest work and routine success, but avoid shortcuts, show-off decisions, and risky promises. Aadal Yoga is shown from 09:47:19 to 05:57:48, so after the Nakshatra change, keep your ego in check.Choghadiya inauspicious slots give extra caution. During the day, Kaal @ 05:56, Rog @ 08:49, Udveg @ 10:16, and Kaal @ 16:02 are not the best for beginnings. At night, Udveg @ 19:02, Rog @ 25:16, and Kaal @ 26:50 also call for restraint. Keep your wallet closed today in these patches, and keep your temper quieter than usual.Rahu Kaal Timings Across India Rahu Kaal Timings Across IndiaRahu Kaal changes from place to place across India because it is calculated using local sunrise, and sunrise differs by longitude even within the same state. That’s why the time you see for one location won’t exactly match another, even on the same date. The table below shows Rahu Kaal for major Indian cities, so you can follow the timing that fits your location accurately.City Rahu Kaal Mumbai 09:28 - 10:55Delhi (NCR) 09:14 - 10:40Bengaluru 09:07 - 10:36Hyderabad 09:05 - 10:33Chennai 08:56 - 10:25Ahmedabad 09:30 - 10:57Pune 09:23 - 10:51Kolkata 08:27 - 09:54Jaipur 09:19 - 10:45Kochi 09:11 - 10:40Lucknow 08:58 - 10:25Indore 09:17 - 10:44Guwahati 08:15 - 09:41Chandigarh 09:16 - 10:41Surat 09:29 - 10:56Visakhapatnam 08:46 - 10:13Nagpur 09:04 - 10:31Coimbatore 09:09 - 10:38Varanasi 08:49 - 10:16Bhubaneswar 08:36 - 10:04Sunrise, Sunset, Moonrise & Moonset Sunrise, Sunset, Moonrise & MoonsetSunrise today is at 05:56:54, and sunset is at 17:29:02. These two points are like the day’s natural gatekeepers. Sunrise isn’t just about light, it sets the inner clock too. If you wake up close to sunrise, the mind feels cleaner and less reactive. Try to do at least one mindful act after 05:56:54, a short prayer, a glass of water, or a few stretches. It sets the tone.Sunset at 17:29:02 is a gentle reminder to slow down. As the light fades, so does the day’s outward push. This is why evening sandhya time feels soothing. Even if you don’t do a full ritual, lighting a lamp or sitting quietly for five minutes can bring steadiness.Moonrise is at 11:46:10 AM and moonset is at 10:23:33 PM. With the Moon in Sagittarius, emotions may feel more expressive after the Moon rises. You may want to speak your mind, plan travel, or dream bigger than usual. It’s inspiring, yes, but don’t turn every idea into a commitment. As the Moon heads toward setting at 10:23:33 PM, the mind tends to review the day. Give yourself a soft landing. Reduce screen time, avoid late-night arguments, and let the nervous system cool down before sleep.Vrat/Festival Information & Recommendations Vrat/Festival Information & RecommendationsNo major Vrat or festival is observed today. The Hindu month is Ashvina (Amanta), a month known for sharpening devotion and cleaning up routines, both outside and within. Even without a festival marker, the Panchang shows a day that asks for careful effort. Mula Nakshatra in the morning is especially good for removing what no longer serves you. That can be as practical as deleting unused apps, clearing old receipts, or finally fixing that small household issue you keep ignoring.For relationships, keep your tone respectful, even if you feel others are not being fair. Sagittarius Moon can make you blunt, and Atiganda Yoga can make people touchy. Choose clarity, not sharpness. If you must address a misunderstanding, do it with simple words, not long lectures. Ask one honest question and then listen. That’s enough.For work and career, today rewards steady follow-through. Your boss will notice quiet reliability more than dramatic last-minute heroics. During Rahu Kaal, chant “Om Raam Rahave Namaha” and keep your mind steady.The day is like a field after rain. Soft, but it can get messy if you rush. Walk carefully. articles.title: Vaping: Why people who have never smoked are getting hooked
articles.summary: More than one million people now vape who have never been smokers, according to the ONS.
articles.body:
When vaping first took off at Gracey Mungulu's school, she was vocal about the fact she found it as repulsive as smoking.

"I literally used to tell people like, 'Er, why are you doing that?'" she says.

But Gracey says the habit became so common among her classmates that by the age of 16 she too had taken it up, even though the first time left her coughing rather than inhaling.

"The more you see it, the more you start trying it a bit more," Gracey says, "and then eventually I just got used to it and I was just doing it all the time."

Now 21, she buys a refillable vape every day, using it whenever her hands aren't busy with her work as a hairdresser and in a school.

Gracey is among the more than one million people in the UK who say they have never smoked but now vape, according to recent Office for National Statistics (ONS) survey data – and that number has risen year-on-year.

When vaping first came to the market it was seen as a way to help smokers quit cigarettes.

Vaping nicotine, a highly addictive substance, is less harmful than cigarettes, but the long-term effects are not yet clear, according to the NHS.

So why are people like Gracey, who have never smoked a cigarette, taking it up?

The Londoner believes vaping helps when she's feeling socially anxious.

"It's the hand action," she says, "just having something in your hand, just having something in your mouth."

Like cigarettes Gracey's vape contains nicotine, a highly addictive substance that triggers withdrawal symptoms like irritability and anxiety when it leaves your system.

Vaping has become a "mindless action," she says. When she answers the call to talk to BBC News for this article, Gracey says that without thinking about it, she had been lying in bed, with her vape in one hand, and her other hand scrolling Instagram.

The habitual aspect of regular vaping is something GP Dr Helen Wall hears a lot from her patients.

"It's that kind of psychological dependence on something else to almost regulate their emotions," she says.

Like Gracey, Malin Andersson, who vaped until recently, says her habit went hand in hand with doomscrolling.

She had also tried cigarettes but never considered herself a smoker.

At 33, she falls in the age range most likely to vape. The ONS report suggests nearly one in six people aged 25-34 in the UK may use e-cigarettes daily or occasionally.

The domestic abuse campaigner and former Love Island contestant started vaping when she was going through a stressful break-up and looking for comfort. She believes it was the physical action that got her hooked.

"It's a dopamine hit," Malin says. "It's literally an adult's version of a dummy."

She says it was dulling her senses and leaving her demotivated.

Malin became so frustrated with how reliant she had become on her banana ice-flavoured vape that she quit in May this year.

"It was annoying me so much that it was always in my hand that I'd end up throwing it across the room," she says.

Alex, from Manchester, also gradually formed a vaping habit, which started after she occasionally vaped on nights out and then began to take the vapes home.

The 26-year-old, who didn't want to give her last name, says the habit would become such a constant part of her life that she would work while "lying in my bed with my laptop in front of me and then my vape on my chest".

Prof Sarah Jackson, from the University College London Alcohol and Tobacco Research Group, points out that while "alarm bells" may ring at the recent ONS figures, it could be the case that some of the people in this group would have started smoking if they hadn't started vaping.

"In which case, vaping has diverted them away from a more harmful behaviour, which is good news," she says. "On the other hand, there will be people that are being exposed to more risk than they would have otherwise."

She points to a 2024 study from UCL researchers that found nicotine use had risen among young adults in England, although cigarette smoking had declined.

"We can infer from that that some of the people who are vaping wouldn't have smoked otherwise," Jackson says.

The ONS report says about 5.4 million people aged 16 and over vape in Britain, while the number of smokers of all ages continues to steadily fall. Some 4.9 million adults in the UK smoke.

The UK is aiming to cut smoking rates and reduce the appeal of vaping among children and young people.

The marketing of vapes - which has featured bright colours and sweet flavours - is being looked at, with a recent government consultation on new measures expected to give a response in due course.

Within the 1.1 million vapers who never smoked, "there probably is a group who would not be vaping [without] the marketing of vaping which is very prominent", says Hazel Cheeseman from charity Action on Smoking and Health.

The NHS warns non-smokers and those aged 17 and under to never vape, while it's illegal for anyone under 18 to buy vapes. Disposable vapes - seen as a key driver in the rise of youth vaping – were banned last year .

Wall says the heavy marketing of vapes in recent years has helped to fuel a "misconception" that they are "safe and not addictive".

Gracey thinks vapes should be sold in the same standardised plain packaging as cigarettes because it "looks scary".

"With vapes, they have all these flavours, all these pretty colours - it's just making us more attracted to it".

While she says vaping is seen as far more socially acceptable among her generation than smoking, she finds her habit problematic and has considered quitting to save the £35 a week it costs her.

But just like smoking, giving up vaping can be a struggle. And for Alex, vaping led her in the opposite direction.

She says she managed to quit vaping while travelling for several months, but with no access to vapes she began smoking cigarettes for the first time instead.

Cigarettes are not considered a healthy or helpful way to stop vaping by experts. The NHS strongly advises people to stop smoking, and it remains the leading cause of preventable illness and premature death in the UK.

To quit vaping the NHS suggests gradually reducing the strength of the vape's nicotine, increasing the time between vaping sessions, or switching to a suitable nicotine replacement therapy product.

But professional support to stop vaping is patchy, with a recent survey finding fewer than half (45%) of healthcare providers in England offered vaping cessation support. There is a mixed picture of support to quit across the rest of the UK.

While it is good fewer people are smoking, Wall says that for people like Gracey who go straight to vapes a bit of the messaging has been missed. "Vaping was only intended [by the NHS] to be a replacement for cigarettes."

articles.title: 'Been more than 10 hours': CJP claims Abhijeet Dipke 'kidnapped' by Delhi Police
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) early Saturday claimed that its founder Abhijeet Dipke had been \"kidnapped\" by Delhi Police.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) early Saturday claimed that its founder Abhijeet Dipke had been "kidnapped" by Delhi Police. CJP's Ajinkya Shinde alleged that more than 10 hours after he was detained, neither his family, lawyers nor party members had been informed about his whereabouts.In a post on X, CJP said it had received no updates on Dipke's location since he was picked up by police ahead of the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' protest.Dipke was detained from Jhandewalan while on his way to Connaught Place, police sources told news agency PTI.. The CJP alleged that he had been taken to an undisclosed location and was not being allowed to speak to lawyers."The Delhi Police has taken Abhijeet Dipke to an undisclosed location. We have lost contact with him. He is not being allowed to talk to lawyers," the party said in an earlier post on X.The party also wrote to the station house officer of Mandir Marg police station, seeking details of Dipke's whereabouts, the legal provisions invoked and the grounds for his preventive detention. CJP leader Rohan Deshpande urged police to disclose who had ordered the detention and ensure Dipke had access to legal counsel and could contact his colleagues.The developments came amid concerns over the detention of All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora, whose whereabouts were also uncertain for several hours. AISA later said its lawyers had traced her to the RK Puram police station around midnight, after she was allegedly moved between locations across Delhi.CPI(ML) Liberation also demanded the immediate release of Dipke, Bora and other detained protesters. CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas called on Delhi Police to disclose the location of detained protesters and explain the grounds for their detention.Police said around 150 people had been detained as part of efforts to maintain law and order and ensure smooth traffic movement. articles.title: Oregon school shooter was former special needs student, police say
articles.summary: A teacher fought teenage shooter and a parent shot him dead, police say on Friday, a day after four people were killed.
articles.body:
The 16-year-old who killed three children and a teacher at an elementary school in the US state of Oregon was a former special-needs student at the school, police and school officials have said.

Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz identified the attacker on Friday, a day after the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School, as Griffin J. John II.

He said the teenager attacked a classroom of special-needs students, where all the victims were shot.

Steven Cook, superintendent of Bend-La Pine Schools, said John was not enrolled in the local public school system at the time.

“That classroom was a special needs classroom, and the suspect was a special needs student in that school,” Cook told a news conference.

Krantz said John shot his way through locked doors with a 12-gauge shotgun, firing as many as 15 shots, and had about 44 rounds left when he was killed. Police are still trying to determine how he obtained the gun.

Under Oregon law, a minor may possess a shotgun if provided by a parent or with a parent’s consent.

The shooter’s mother, Shauntai Nickerson, separately told reporters outside her apartment: “I’m so sorry, I wish I could have done something.”

A teacher threw her phone at the gunman, then tackled and fought him, likely saving lives, Krantz said, calling her actions “heroic”. She was not injured.

A 36-year-old father, Kaylub Giamanco, who has two children at the school, then followed the gunman inside and shot him dead minutes after the first 911 call.

US President Donald Trump called Giamanco a “great hero”. “It’s a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it,” Trump said.

The children killed were aged five, eight and 11, and the teacher was Meghan Lambert, 25, police said.

A seven-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to hospital in critical condition.

The shooting is the 28th mass killing in the US this year, according to a database by The Associated Press, USA Today and Northeastern University.

The Gun Violence Archive in the US has documented 369 mass shootings in 2026, defined as incidents in which four or more people are shot.

The Everytown for Gun Safety group has counted at least 100 incidents of gunfire on school grounds this year, with 34 deaths.
